articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning across text, image, audio, and video inputs with a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates substantial improvements in long-horizon planning tasks and complex code generation, with benchmarks showing near-expert performance on graduate-level STEM problems. Enterprise API availability began rolling out in late April with tiered pricing based on context utilization.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Agentic Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on agentic task-completion benchmarks including SWE-bench and WebArena, demonstrating the ability to autonomously navigate multi-step software engineering and web-based workflows. The model integrates a refined mixture-of-experts architecture with improved tool-use grounding. Google is positioning the model as the backbone for its Workspace AI agents rolling out across enterprise customers.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoid in BMW Plants
articles.summary: Figure Robotics announced that its Figure 03 humanoid robot has entered commercial deployment at two BMW manufacturing facilities in South Carolina, performing parts kitting, material transport, and light assembly tasks alongside human workers. The robots leverage on-device vision-language models for real-time task adaptation without explicit reprogramming. This marks one of the first scaled commercial deployments of general-purpose humanoid robots in automotive manufacturing.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Electric Demonstrates Autonomous Disaster Response in DARPA Trial
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics showcased its electric Atlas robot completing a full autonomous disaster-response course as part of a DARPA evaluation, including navigating rubble, opening valves, and carrying a 40-pound payload up degraded stairs. The system used no teleoperation, relying entirely on onboard perception and planning stacks. The trial represents a significant milestone toward certifying humanoid platforms for real-world emergency deployment.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional Classifiers for Real-Time LLM Output Safety Filtering
articles.summary: Anthropic published research and released an open-source toolkit for constitutional classifiers — lightweight neural classifiers trained via constitutional AI principles that can screen LLM outputs in real time with sub-10ms latency overhead. The approach reduces harmful output rates by over 90% on adversarial red-team benchmarks while preserving helpfulness scores. The toolkit is model-agnostic and designed to be integrated into any serving pipeline.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that its A14 (1.4nm-class) gate-all-around nanosheet process has entered volume production at its Fab 20 facility in Tainan, with initial wafers shipping to lead customers including Apple and NVIDIA. The node delivers approximately 20% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2, targeting next-generation AI accelerator and mobile SoC designs. Yield rates are reportedly ahead of internal targets, which could accelerate broader customer adoption in H2 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly announced that their trapped-ion quantum system has achieved fault-tolerant operations on logical qubits with error rates below the threshold required for practical quantum error correction, sustaining a logical error rate of 10⁻⁶ across 100 consecutive rounds of syndrome extraction. This milestone moves the industry closer to building reliable, scalable quantum computers capable of tackling problems in materials science and cryptography.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Phase Begins with First Compliance Audits of Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European AI Office has initiated its first formal compliance audits under the EU AI Act's provisions for general-purpose AI models, with OpenAI, Google, and Meta among the companies receiving audit notifications. The audits focus on systemic risk assessments, compute reporting thresholds, and red-teaming documentation requirements for models exceeding 10²⁵ FLOPs of training compute. The outcome of these audits will set important precedents for how the Act's most consequential provisions are interpreted in practice.
